english.title: Wilfully give false information concerning the registration of a birth / death
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) wilfully gave to a registrar of births or deaths false information, namely **(..SPECIFY THE FALSIFICATION..), concerning the

(A)_[birth of **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[death of **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(C)_[cause of the death of **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(D)_[death and cause of the death of **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4(1)(a) of the Perjury Act 1911.

english.notes:
(i) Statutory requirement for corroboration (section 13).
(ii) A prosecution on indictment for an offence against this section shall not be commenced more than three years after the commission of the offence. (section 4(2)).
(iii) Summary proceedings - six months Time Limit on Prosecution. Proceedings on indictment - three years Time Limit on Prosecution.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
